record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions in neutrino-induced quasi-elastic scattering and single photon production
record.original_question: What remaining neutral-current single-photon production mechanisms, especially anomalous ωZγ contributions with large theoretical uncertainties, and what direct measurements by MicroBooNE, MINERvA, ND280/T2K, or similar detectors are needed to make this background sufficiently controlled for electron-neutrino appearance studies?

evidence.quote:
Overall, the situation for neutrino NC γ production seems to be converging
and under control. The theoretical models agree with the experimentally de-
termined predictions for this process as determined by MiniBooNE. However,
there are possible contributions, namely from the anomalous ωZγ term, where
theoretical uncertainties remain large and the calculation is not robust.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider neutral-current (NC) single-photon production in neutrino–nucleus scattering, i.e. processes of the form ν + N → ν + γ + X, which constitute an irreducible background to electron-neutrino appearance searches in accelerator-based oscillation experiments. Standard contributions include NC Δ(1232) radiative decay, non-resonant nucleon-pole and meson-exchange amplitudes, and NC coherent photon production on nuclei. In addition, the chiral anomaly induces an "anomalous" ωZγ vertex (analogous to the ωγγ Wess–Zumino–Witten term), giving an ω-meson-exchange contribution to NC γ production whose normalization, off-shell behavior, and nuclear modification carry large theoretical uncertainties.

Identify and quantify:
(a) the remaining NC single-photon production mechanisms—most importantly the anomalous ωZγ contribution—that are not yet under firm theoretical control, providing a robust calculation of their cross sections (flux-averaged differential and total) on nucleon and nuclear targets in the sub-GeV to few-GeV neutrino energy range, with quantified theoretical uncertainties; and
(b) the direct experimental measurements of NC γ production (exclusive single-photon final states, separated into resonant, non-resonant/anomalous, and coherent components) achievable with detectors such as MicroBooNE (liquid argon TPC at the Booster Neutrino Beam), MINERvA, and ND280/T2K, that are required to constrain these mechanisms at a level sufficient (typically ≲10–20% on the total NC γ rate in the relevant kinematic region) for this background to no longer limit νe appearance / sterile-neutrino searches.

The problem is to determine what theoretical refinements and experimental measurements are needed, and at what precision, so that the NC single-photon background — including the anomalous ωZγ piece — is rendered "sufficiently controlled" for current and next-generation electron-neutrino appearance studies.
artifact.status_search_result: MicroBooNE has since published several direct measurements of NC single-photon production: a search for NC Δ radiative decay placing a 90% CL bound of <2.3× the nominal rate (PRL 128, 111801, 2022), a first search for NC coherent single-photon production (arXiv:2502.06091, 2025), and an inclusive anomalous single-photon search (arXiv:2502.06064, 2025). These directly address the experimental program called for, but a definitive measurement isolating the anomalous ωZγ contribution and reducing its theoretical uncertainty has not yet been achieved; work on MINERvA and ND280/T2K is ongoing. Hence the question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Search for NC Δ radiative decay in MicroBooNE
status_evidence.snippet: Bound on anomalous enhancement of NC Δ radiative decay <2.3× nominal at 90% CL.
status_evidence.claim: MicroBooNE has performed a direct measurement constraining the dominant NC single-photon channel.

status_evidence.title: Inclusive Search for Anomalous Single-Photon Production in MicroBooNE
status_evidence.snippet: Inclusive search for anomalous single-photon production from neutrino interactions in MicroBooNE.
status_evidence.claim: Direct experimental measurements of NC γ production in LAr-TPCs are now being delivered.

status_evidence.title: First Search for Neutral Current Coherent Single-Photon Production in MicroBooNE
status_evidence.snippet: First search for NC coherent single-photon production in MicroBooNE.
status_evidence.claim: The coherent NC γ channel has now received a first dedicated experimental search.
